title: Auto-fallback playbook and edge-case runbook for rollouts console
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note is a focused playbook for designing the automatic fallback (auto-fallback) experience in the Rollouts Console. Covers UI flows, microcopy, simulation previews, edge cases, and a short runbook for SRE/CS to use when fallback triggers.

Context (why this exists):
- Rollouts console currently supports canary and A/B traffic targeting but lacks a clear, testable auto-fallback composer and visualizer.
- Teams need a predictable way to specify fallback policies for model degradation, latency regressions, and capacity constraints.
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic: proposals + UI sketches + a checklist for implementation and QA.

High-level goals:
- Make fallback policy authoring simple: concise predicates, clear precedence, and safe defaults.
- Provide deterministic simulation and in-console dry-run for common traffic shapes.
- Surface immediate impact (estimated QPS, cost delta, expected latency change) before saving.
- Provide robust observability hooks and an on-call-friendly runbook when fallback engages.

Primary user journeys to support:
1) Create a canary with an automatic fallback: author a canary (5% traffic) -> attach auto-fallback policy -> run simulation -> save.
2) Add fallback to existing A/B experiment: choose variant B fallback to variant A when latency > X or error rate > Y.
3) Emergency safe-mode toggle: ops flips an immediate fallback to a lower-cost/stable variant for a route.
4) Diagnostic drill-in: when fallback fires, open timeline, see traces and the evaluated predicates.

Policy composer: fields and UX notes
- Policy name (free text): microcopy "Descriptive and unique, e.g. 'latency-95-fallback-to-v1'"
- Trigger conditions (one or more):
  - Error rate over window: numeric + unit (e.g. 5% over 2m)
  - P95/P99 latency over window: ms threshold + window
  - Model inference failures (decoder errors, GPU OOM) : toggle + example log messages
  - Throughput saturation: queue depth or rejected requests count
  - Custom signal: tag-based (user-provided metric) with a documentation link placeholder
- Precedence: radio selection (soft failover vs hard redirect). Explanation microcopy: "Soft: mirror traffic while returning canonical variant for production; Hard: route matching traffic immediately to fallback."
- Cooldown and evaluation window: numeric (seconds/minutes) + explanation text.
- Rollback action: automatic rollback? (yes/no) + safe rollback window
- Notification targets: Slack / PagerDuty / Email (multi-select)
- Simulation toggle: checkbox "Run a dry-run simulation using recent traffic snapshot"

Composer UX details and microcopy
- Inline help: small question mark icons with one-sentence clarifications. Example: "P95 over 2m: fraction of requests finishing within the 95th percentile over a 2-minute rolling window."
- Validation: prevent conflicting triggers (e.g., identical trigger with different precedence) with a red toast: "Conflicting rules detected — please consolidate or set precedence."
- Auto-suggestions: when user types latency thresholds, suggest common thresholds derived from recent route metrics (populate a suggested list).

Simulation and preview panel (right rail)
- Inputs: time window (default last 15m), traffic slice (all routes / single route / user segment), simulation speed selector (sample / full)
- Outputs shown as simple strings for quick scan:
  - Expected engaged fallback QPS: "~12 qps (1.8% of traffic)"
  - Estimated cost delta: "+$0.03/min while active"
  - Estimated latency change (median/P95): "median +2ms, p95 -30ms"
  - Trigger probability: "Policy would have fired 3 times in last 24h (last: 2026-02-18 14:12 UTC)"
- Visual: a tiny sparkline (thumbnail) and a simulated timeline list (timestamp + trigger cause)
- If sample unavailable -> show graceful message: "Not enough recent traffic to run a representative simulation."

Wireframe sketch (quick ASCII)
- Left: Policy composer (form)
- Right: Simulation preview + impact summary + quick 'save as draft' and 'apply (staged)' buttons
- Top: Route selector + rollout percentage editor

Edge cases and how the UI should handle them
1) Incompatible model variants: when user picks fallback variant with incompatible schema (e.g., different tokenization), show blocking warning: "Selected fallback uses an incompatible model tokenizer — responses may be malformed. Confirm to continue."
2) Partial metrics availability: if target route lacks P99 metrics, disable P99 trigger and show 'use P95 instead' suggestion.
3) Conflicting active policies: when a new policy overlaps with existing policies, present merge/precedence modal listing affected policies and proposed resolution. Include a 'preview effective policy' checkbox.
4) Overlapping A/B experiments: explicitly show traffic partitioning and ensure total percentages sum to 100% before allowing hard fallback.
5) Rapid flip-flopping: implement a built-in hysteresis (min 60s between toggles) and expose it in the policy composer.

Runbook (ops steps when fallback fires)
- Automated alert triggers: Slack + PD + in-console banner
- Quick triage steps:
  1) Open Rollouts -> Route -> Fallback timeline. Note the evaluated predicate and sample traces.
  2) If error rate spike: check upstream infra (GPU logs) and recent deploys (linked GitHub PR in timeline).
  3) If fallback was to cheaper variant -> re-evaluate quality regression via 'sample compare' (console feature)
  4) If fallback persisted > 15m, escalate to Eng-on-call to consider temporary circuit-breaker or increase capacity.
- Postmortem pointer: run a canned template (link: CONFLUENCE-9876)

Observability hooks to add to the console (implementation checklist)
- Show exact predicate evaluation results for each trigger (list of boolean checks + raw metric values).
- Link to traces: pre-filtered APM query (time window + route + request id sample).
- Attach example request/response pairs (anonymized) to help triage model correctness issues.
- Audit log entry with full policy JSON and the traffic snapshot used to evaluate the policy.

Accessibility and microcopy guardrails
- Avoid technical acronyms in labels where possible; use tooltips to explain.
- Make severity language human-friendly: "error rate" vs "http 5xx" should both be selectable but presented clearly.
- Color semantics: red = active failure/fallback engaged; amber = policy armed but not triggered; green = healthy. Provide non-color indicators (icons) for colorblind users.

Open questions and decisions for engineering/product
- Do we support AND/OR compound predicates in the first iteration, or only OR (any trigger)? Suggest OR-only for v1, add compound predicates later.
- What is the canonical simulation dataset size? default 15 minutes or last N requests? (Engineering input needed)
- Should 'soft' fallback mirror or shadow traffic to fallback? This has cost implications and privacy implications (mirroring sample payloads).
- How to surface model output quality changes automatically? Need an ML signal integration (score baseline) to compare outputs.

QA checklist for rollout
- [ ] Composer validation: all fields enforce ranges and show inline errors.
- [ ] Simulation accuracy: simulation UI matches a backend dry-run endpoint and returns identical timestamps.
- [ ] Precedence modal tests for 3 overlapping policies.
- [ ] Accessibility: keyboard navigation, ARIA labels, contrast checks.
- [ ] Runbook automation: Slack and PD alerts fire with correct payloads.

Implementation notes (engineering hints)
- Backend: store policies as versioned JSON blobs with schema v1. Track evaluation metadata separately so policy edits don't mutate historical executions.
- Telemetry: log (policy_id, evaluated_time, predicate_snapshot, decided_action, traffic_snapshot_id) to a time-series store for quick UI queries.
- Simulation: use sampled recent traffic (first-class API) with deterministic replay for consistent simulation outputs.

Unresolved UX microcopy snippets (drafts)
- Save button: "Save and stage (apply at next rollout window)"
- Immediate apply: "Apply now — override staged settings"
- Soft fallback label: "Soft degrade (mirror + fallback)" tooltip: "Mirror requests to fallback while returning verified variant to users for short-term diagnosis"
- Hard fallback label: "Immediate redirect (stop sending traffic to variant)"

Next steps and owners
- Product: refine microcopy, finalize v1 scope (Priya)
- Applied ML: evaluate feasibility of automated quality delta signals (Aisha)
- Backend: schema + evaluation API design (Marco)
- SRE: validate alerting semantics and playbook (Tom)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally a working doc. Expect lots of follow-ups. Please add comments inline or drop short notes in the linked Confluence thread (CONFLUENCE-9876).

Quick links for prototyping
- Sketch file (design): github.com/redwood/designs/rollouts/auto-fallback-sketch (work-in-progress)
- Example policy JSON (minimal):
  {
    "policy_name": "p95-latency-fallback",
    "trigger": "p95>600ms for 2m",
    "action": "redirect-to:v1"
  }

Changelog
- 2025-11-03: initial draft (Priya)
- 2026-01-07: added simulation panel spec and runbook bullets (Marco)
- 2026-02-22: refined edge cases and QA checklist (Aisha)
